newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower despite high-tech rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower despite high-tech rise.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Wednesday despite a modest rise in the electronics sector as investors took profits against a modest recent rebound. Brokers noted a conspicuous lack of broad-market confidence.
The weighted index stayed lower all session before closing 64.80 points or 0.80 percent down at 8,058.46.
Turnover once again was modest at just T$81.13 billion.
The index had gained nearly 200 points since May 15 before losing 71.40 points on Tuesday and dropping again on Wednesday.
Wednesday's fall came despite a 0.78 percent electronics rise spurred partly by Wall Street's overnight high-tech gains.
"All the funds were concentrated too heavily in electronic stocks, especially integrated-circuit shares," said David Yu, vice president of International Investment Trust.
"Such a disparity meant that confidence in the market was weak other than in just the one sector," said Yu.
The electronic sector fielded the session's five most heavily traded shares. Chipmaker Winbond, which notched the session's highest trade volume at 84.7 million shares, dropped T$0.90 to T$38.
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co gained T$5 to T$116 ahead of its ex-rights date on June 12.
The heavily weighted financial sector lost 1.31 percent on profit-taking. Foods and papers dropped 1.46 percent and 2.25 percent, respectively.
Brokers said they expected the market to continue a slow descend on Thursday while struggling to stay above the 8,000-point support level.
